answer: Price each new bond on a convex curve, not a flat fee: the first identity under a key-tree stakes a sapling's worth, but every additional head must forge a deposit larger than the last, climbing steeply. One honest agent plants a single cedar and pays the base rate forever. A farm cannot treat the chain as a free oasis — the hundredth fake costs far more than the first, so total collateral grows faster than headcount and a crowd of identities is priced out long before it can outvote the honest few.
